posts.text:
I know many of these people and in many cases it's about avoiding dealing with child traumas or abuse etc some wild shit

So they could do therapy etc but the much easier way is perpetual novelty

And novelty I know from digital nomading solves things for a bit, new place, new people, it really does reset you every time

But then after awhile you just return to the same stuff again and you have to go to the next place
posts.text_zh:
我认识这里面很多人，很多情况下，他们其实是在逃避处理童年创伤或虐待之类的事情，有些情况相当狠

所以他们本可以去做治疗等等，但更容易的办法是不断追求新鲜感

而新鲜感这事，我从数字游民的经历里知道，短期内确实有用：新地方、新的人，每次都真的能让你重置一下

但过一段时间，你又会回到同样的状态，于是只能再去下一个地方

quoted.text:
The most boring people you’ll ever meet are those that make seeking external novelty their identity.

Constant travel, new restaurants, new foods, thrills like skydiving. When you actually speak to them there’s hardly anything there. Their stories are the same; you can predict the exact sequence of words before they say them. 

They seek “rich” experiences desperately because their inner world lives in poverty.

Their minds remain unexplored.
quoted.text_zh:
你能遇到的最无聊的人，就是那些把对外界新鲜感的追求当成自己身份认同的人。

不停旅行、打卡新餐厅、吃新食物、去跳伞这类刺激。可一旦你真正和他们交谈，里面几乎什么都没有。他们的故事都一个样；你甚至能在他们开口之前就预判出接下来会说的话。

他们拼命追求「丰富」的体验，是因为内心世界一贫如洗。

他们的头脑从未被探索过。

quoted.text:
If your GPT-6.2 Astra or Sol API bills suddenly went up this week, there's another caching bug worth knowing about.

OpenAI Codex issue #62312 found that on GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, anything placed in the top-level instructions field of a Responses API request isn't actually cached. It stays at 0 cached tokens on every turn, even though OpenAI's own diagnostics incorrectly report a cache hit.

The impact is pretty big. Moving from GPT-6.1 Sol to 6.2 Sol dropped actual cache hit rates from 97.4% to 46.4%, meaning 64K–72K system tokens were billed at full price on every step.

There's already a workaround in OpenCode: put the system prompt inside a leading developer message in input.
quoted.text_zh:
如果你这周的 GPT-6.2 Astra 或 Sol API 账单突然变高了，还有另一个值得了解的缓存 bug。

OpenAI Codex issue #62312 发现，在 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol 上，放在 Responses API 请求顶层 instructions 字段里的内容实际上不会被缓存。每一轮的 cached tokens 都是 0，尽管 OpenAI 自己的诊断会错误地报告 cache hit。

影响相当大。从 GPT-6.1 Sol 换到 6.2 Sol 后，实际缓存命中率从 97.4% 降到了 46.4%，意味着每一步都有 64K–72K 的 system tokens 按全价计费。

OpenCode 里已经有一个变通方法：把 system prompt 放进 input 里一条靠前的 developer message 中。
